calls.reason: The evidence is mixed. Cursor's reported negative 23% gross margin fits his story, but Gamma reportedly grew to $100M ARR while profitable and Replit says it is gross margin positive. No evidence tests whether growth depended on the subsidy, which his 'only grew because' requires.

The only pricing evidence is Anthropic's optional premium-priced fast mode, and Sonnet 4.6 kept the same token prices. Nothing links any price change to cash or compute pressure, or shows labs broadly raising prices on startups.

Only one later Anthropic tightening is documented (third-party harness use billed separately from April 4). Anthropic then raised limits in May, and OpenAI cuts are undocumented. The record is incomplete either way.
The forecast's condition has not occurred. StatMuse shows ARM's lowest intraday price in 2026 was $100.02, and the stock traded above $200 in late October, never below $80.

Forbes (via The Decoder) reported Cursor's business plans as profitable, and TechCrunch's source said large enterprise sales had positive gross margins. Both sources are weak, but his counter-evidence is only anecdotes from unnamed customers about what they 'can' burn.

Reports confirm the March 13–27 off-peak promotion and the peak-hour cuts announced March 26. But 'muddies the water' is a judgement call, and the only sign of confusion is one GitHub bug report, with no before-and-after measure.
